patch.value: Preserve UTF-16 surrogate cuts in bounded JSON list output

Synthetic 2026.10.5 differential finding from pm-rust-ufzy: a title made from 239 ASCII characters, one astral Unicode character, and a long ASCII suffix crosses the published 240 UTF-16-unit string compaction boundary. The TS CLI emits the lone high surrogate as an escaped JSON code unit; the native serde_json Value representation emits a Unicode replacement character instead. This also changes bounded token receipts. A representation or serialization change is required for full parity at that boundary.

Both real CLIs emit byte-identical bounded JSON and token estimates when compaction cuts an astral character at unit 240; SDK serialization preserves the same contract; Existing four-metric 100 percent coverage and documentation gates remain enforced

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Reproduction evidence: a synthetic single-item title of 239 ASCII x characters, one emoji, and 2000 more x characters was read with list --json --full --output-budget 500 by both real executables. The reference emits an escaped high surrogate at the cut; native serde_json emits a replacement character. In the observed fixture the read-output estimates were 424 versus 423 tokens. The boundary and reproduction are documented in docs/LIST_PAGINATION_2026_10_5.md.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The reproduced Unicode boundary is explicitly documented in draft PR https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rust/pull/60 and docs/LIST_PAGINATION_2026_10_5.md. Full parity is not claimed for this case; the issue remains open.
